Photo source: Abiy Ahmed Ali / Facebook Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud held talks in Antalya, Türkiye, on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, focusing on Somalia’s security situation, bilateral cooperation and broader developments across the Horn of Africa. The meeting took place ahead of the COP31 Leaders’ Summit, bringing the two leaders together amid continuing diplomatic efforts to strengthen relations between Addis Ababa and Mogadishu. Prime Minister Abiy said the discussions addressed the evolving security situation in Somalia and regional developments, emphasizing the importance of continued dialogue and cooperation in promoting peace and stability. Somalia’s official SONNA news agency also confirmed the meeting, reporting that the two leaders discussed bilateral relations and issues of mutual interest, including regional security. Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation and advancing shared prosperity, according to the Somali government report. The discussions come at a time when security challenges across the Horn of Africa remain closely interconnected, particularly Somalia’s continuing fight against Al-Shabaab and the wider diplomatic tensions involving Ethiopia, Eritrea and neighboring countries. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud recently outlined his country’s position on these tensions, stating that Somalia would stay out of any potential military confrontation between Ethiopia and Eritrea. The latest meeting also follows months of diplomatic disagreements involving maritime access, regional security arrangements and the political status of Somaliland. Relations between Ethiopia and Somalia deteriorated in January 2024 after Addis Ababa signed a memorandum of understanding with Somaliland concerning access to the sea. Somalia rejected the agreement, arguing that it violated its sovereignty and territorial integrity. Türkiye subsequently mediated negotiations between the two countries, culminating in the Ankara Declaration on December 11, 2024. Under the declaration, Ethiopia and Somalia reaffirmed their commitment to respecting each other’s sovereignty, unity, independence and territorial integrity while agreeing to pursue mutually beneficial arrangements for Ethiopia’s access to the sea under Somalia’s sovereign authority. The issue remains significant in regional diplomacy, with Ethiopia continuing to emphasize its economic and strategic interests in maritime access. In October, Ethiopia reasserted its interests in the Nile and Red Sea following a declaration adopted by Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia at the Alamein summit. The Ethiopian government’s response emphasized the country’s geographical proximity to the Red Sea and its position that regional maritime discussions should account for Ethiopia’s interests. Wednesday’s meeting between Abiy and Hassan Sheikh therefore comes against a backdrop of competing regional interests, although neither government publicly indicated that the latest talks resulted in a new agreement on maritime access or other disputed issues. The meeting also followed Abiy Ahmed’s discussions with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on November 10, during which the leaders explored opportunities to strengthen bilateral cooperation, address regional developments and coordinate on climate priorities. Türkiye is hosting COP31, while Ethiopia is preparing to assume the COP32 presidency in 2027. According to Prime minister Abiy Ahmed’s Facebook post , Abiy and Hassan Sheikh emphasized sustained dialogue, stronger bilateral cooperation and coordinated efforts to promote regional security and stability. Neither government announced a new bilateral agreement following Wednesday’s discussions. The meeting nevertheless marked another high-level diplomatic engagement between the two neighboring countries as they continue consultations on shared security challenges and regional relations. Continue Reading Ethiopia Ethiopia Links Nile Water Talks to Egypt’s Support for Red Sea Access Ethiopian minister connects Nile negotiations with maritime access ambitions. Published 3 days ago on November 8, 2026 By Kulu Media News Desk An aerial view of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on Ethiopia's Blue Nile River. Ethiopia's water minister has linked prospects for understanding with Egypt over Nile water management to support for Ethiopia's Red Sea access ambitions. Photo: GERD Ethiopia has raised the prospect of linking negotiations over Nile River water management to Egypt’s support for its pursuit of Red Sea access, introducing another contentious issue into an already strained diplomatic relationship between Addis Ababa and Cairo. Ethiopian Minister of Water and Energy Habtamu Itefa said Egypt should help Ethiopia secure access to the sea, suggesting that such cooperation could create an opportunity for understanding over the Nile dispute. Speaking in an interview broadcast by Al Arabiya , Habtamu presented Ethiopia’s maritime ambitions and Nile water development as strategic interests that Egypt should recognize. The remarks, reported on November 5, represent a significant expansion of Ethiopia’s diplomatic argument, connecting two issues that have increasingly shaped political and security relations across the Horn of Africa. Egypt, however, has maintained that negotiations over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) should focus on a legally binding framework protecting the water security of downstream countries. The disagreement comes amid growing regional tensions involving Ethiopia, Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan, whose leaders have taken increasingly divergent positions on Nile water management and Red Sea governance. In October, Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia adopted an Alamein joint declaration reaffirming their positions on regional sovereignty, Nile water security and responsibility for governing the Red Sea. Habtamu’s latest remarks suggest that Addis Ababa is seeking greater recognition of its maritime interests alongside its right to develop water resources originating within Ethiopian territory. In a separate interview with Fana Media Corporation , the minister criticized Egypt’s approach to Nile water negotiations and argued that Ethiopia’s environmental and infrastructure investments benefit downstream countries. He said Ethiopia had planted more than 56 billion trees over the past seven to eight years, including in the Abbay, Tekeze and Baro river basins, contributing to watershed conservation and water availability. Habtamu argued that Egypt should acknowledge those efforts rather than accuse Ethiopia of threatening its water security. The minister also criticized Egypt’s cultivation of water-intensive crops, particularly rice and sugarcane, saying Cairo should reconsider its own water consumption practices. Those claims reflect Ethiopia’s position in the dispute and do not establish that Egypt’s water shortages are primarily caused by agricultural practices. Habtamu maintained that Ethiopia does not intend to prevent Nile waters from reaching downstream countries, while insisting that the country will continue developing its rivers for electricity generation, irrigation and economic growth. He also rejected the idea that Ethiopia requires approval from Egypt or any other country to construct dams within its sovereign territory. In another Fana interview , Habtamu described the GERD as a symbol of national sovereignty and said Ethiopia would continue pursuing additional water infrastructure projects. The GERD, built on the Blue Nile near Ethiopia’s border with Sudan, remains central to the dispute. Ethiopia considers the project essential for expanding electricity generation and supporting national development, while Egypt and Sudan have repeatedly sought enforceable arrangements governing its operation. The latest disagreement follows a joint meeting of Egyptian and Sudanese foreign and irrigation ministers in Cairo on November 2. In their official joint declaration , the two governments reaffirmed their opposition to what they described as unilateral Ethiopian actions in the Eastern Nile Basin. They argued that the absence of a binding legal framework for operating the GERD creates continuing risks for downstream water security. Egypt and Sudan also emphasized their existing water allocations under the 1959 Nile Waters Agreement and called for renewed cooperation based on prior notification, consultation and the prevention of significant harm. Ethiopia is not a party to the 1959 agreement between Egypt and Sudan and has long rejected the argument that historical allocations can restrict its own development rights. The countries also remain divided over the Nile Basin Cooperative Framework Agreement, which Ethiopia supports as a mechanism for more inclusive management of the river’s resources. Egypt and Sudan have not joined that framework and continue to seek arrangements addressing their concerns about existing water uses and future development projects. The Cairo declaration also addressed the Red Sea, asserting that responsibility for its governance belongs to countries bordering the waterway. Egypt and Sudan opposed maritime arrangements for landlocked countries that would undermine the sovereignty, territorial integrity or security of coastal states. Their position does not amount to a rejection of every form of commercial port access for landlocked countries, but it places clear conditions on how such access should be negotiated. Ethiopia, which has been landlocked since Eritrea’s independence in 1993, has repeatedly identified reliable maritime access as a national economic and strategic priority. The issue has already complicated its relationships with several neighboring governments. Ethiopia’s January 2024 memorandum of understanding with Somaliland generated strong objections from Somalia, which regards Somaliland as part of its sovereign territory. The dispute was subsequently addressed through Turkish-mediated negotiations and the December 2024 Ankara Declaration. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has since said his government is prepared to discuss Ethiopian sea access through arrangements that respect Somalia’s sovereignty and internationally accepted procedures. Meanwhile, Ethiopia’s pursuit of maritime access has become a major issue in its deteriorating relations with Eritrea. Ethiopian officials have continued calling for regional cooperation on maritime security, including proposals for collective Red Sea security , while tensions between Addis Ababa and Asmara remain high. The broader diplomatic confrontation has also been accompanied by security allegations. In October, Ethiopia’s military chief accused Eritrea, Egypt and Sudan of supporting TPLF-aligned forces, allegations that have not been independently substantiated. These tensions provide the backdrop to Habtamu’s latest remarks, although no agreement has been announced linking Egyptian support for Ethiopia’s maritime ambitions to a settlement over Nile water management. Cairo has previously rejected reports suggesting that it would trade concessions over the GERD for Ethiopian access to the Red Sea. The latest statements therefore highlight a widening diplomatic disagreement rather than a negotiated arrangement. With Ethiopia continuing to defend its right to develop the Nile and Egypt and Sudan demanding binding protections for downstream water security, the prospect of renewed negotiations remains uncertain. Habtamu’s proposal adds another issue to those talks, raising the question of whether the countries can address their competing water and maritime interests through separate negotiations or a broader regional diplomatic process. In a Facebook post on November 11, 2026, Reda discussed these allegations during a meeting with UN Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa, Guang Cong, focusing on regional security challenges. He claimed that Eritrea and Sudan's involvement in supporting armed groups is destabilizing and must cease for meaningful dialogue to occur. Despite the serious nature of these accusations, Reda emphasized the importance of diplomacy over military action, stating that discussions are preferable to conflict. The allegations, which have not been independently verified, come amid rising tensions in the Horn of Africa, particularly concerning the ongoing conflict in Sudan and Ethiopia's strained relations with its neighbors.

ethiopia.title: G7 Warns of Regional Escalation Risk As Ethiopia-Eritrea Tensions Worsen
ethiopia.content: Eritrea: G7 Warns of Regional Escalation Risk As Ethiopia-Eritrea Tensions Worsen - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Eritrea: G7 Warns of Regional Escalation Risk As Ethiopia-Eritrea Tensions Worsen 11 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — The Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers have expressed concern over worsening tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea, warning that further escalation could destabilize the wider Horn of Africa and threaten regional security, humanitarian operations and international trade, including in the Red Sea. In a joint declaration issued following their meeting in Paris on 9 and 10 November 2026, the foreign ministers said they had noted "with great concern the worsening security situation in the Horn of Africa, specifically between Ethiopia and Eritrea," warning that the situation carried "the risk of regional escalation amid rising cross-border tensions." The ministers cautioned that further escalation could have "serious consequences" for regional stability, already dire humanitarian crises, security and international trade, particularly in the Red Sea, a strategically important maritime corridor. They called on all parties to "exercise maximum restraint, pursue diplomatic solutions" and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, alongside the protection of civilians, particularly women and children. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines The declaration also reaffirmed the importance of respecting "the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of all countries in the region," while expressing support for efforts by the United Nations and African Union to reduce tensions and facilitate dialogue between the parties. The G7 statement comes amid heightened tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea, with relations deteriorating over Ethiopia's longstanding demand for sovereign access to the Red Sea and its stated interest in securing access to the sea through the Eritrean port of Assab. Eritrea has repeatedly rejected any suggestion that its territorial sovereignty could be compromised. The dispute has raised concerns about the possibility of renewed confrontation between the two neighbouring countries, whose relations have remained fragile despite the 2018 peace agreement that formally ended two decades of hostilities following their 1998-2000 border war. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Tells UN Envoy Eritrea, Sudan Backing Armed Groups and Drone Attacks
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia Tells UN Envoy Eritrea, Sudan Backing Armed Groups and Drone Attacks - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia Tells UN Envoy Eritrea, Sudan Backing Armed Groups and Drone Attacks 11 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Ethiopia has accused Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki and Sudan's army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan of supporting, arming and coordinating armed groups operating inside Ethiopia, including through repeated drone attacks, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's Horn of Africa adviser Getachew K. Reda said. Getachew disclosed the accusations following a meeting on Wednesday with Guang Cong, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa, during which they discussed conflicts in Sudan and Somalia, as well as what he described as Eritrea's destabilizing role in the region. In a statement posted on his official social media account, Getachew said he had presented Ethiopia's position on what he described as activities by the Eritrean and Sudanese leadership to equip and coordinate armed elements inside Ethiopia. He also accused them of carrying out repeated drone attacks inside the country. Getachew said he had urged both governments to stop supporting and arming the groups, arguing that doing so was necessary for meaningful dialogue and to prevent further escalation. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn The discussions also addressed prospects for de-escalating the conflict in Sudan, although Getachew did not provide further details of the envoy's response or identify any specific agreements reached during the meeting. The accusations come amid heightened regional tensions involving Ethiopia, Eritrea and Sudan, with Addis Abeba repeatedly raising concerns over alleged external support for armed groups operating inside its territory. Getachew said he and the UN envoy agreed that dialogue rather than military confrontation offered the best path forward, concluding that "talking, not shooting is the best game in town." Editorial note: The allegations against Eritrea and Sudan's military leadership have not been independently verified. The statement did not include responses from Asmara or Khartoum. Getachew's accusations come amid escalating diplomatic tensions between Ethiopia and Sudan, following reciprocal expulsions of diplomatic staff and the closure of consular offices in both countries. On 4 November 2026, Addis Standard reported that Ethiopia had ordered six Sudanese diplomatic staff members to leave the country within 48 hours , following the closure of Sudan's consulate in Assosa, the administrative centre of Benishangul-Gumuz Regional State. A senior Ethiopian official confirmed the expulsions to Reuters but did not disclose the reason for the decision. The following day, Addis Standard reported that Sudan had closed Ethiopia's consulate in the eastern city of Gedaref and ordered Ethiopian diplomatic staff to leave in retaliation for the Assosa closure and the expulsion of Sudanese diplomats. Two Sudanese officials confirmed the reciprocal measures to Reuters. The diplomatic measures came amid competing accusations by the two governments of supporting armed groups operating in each other's territories, adding to concerns over the widening regional tensions. The reciprocal diplomatic measures come days after Sudan's army-aligned government announced that it had lodged formal complaints against Ethiopia with the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and the African Union Peace and Security Council (AUPSC), accusing Addis Abeba of allowing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to use Ethiopian territory to launch drone attacks against civilian infrastructure in Sudan. The move adds another layer to an increasingly volatile diplomatic standoff in which both governments accuse the other of supporting their adversaries. Sudan alleges that Ethiopia is facilitating RSF operations, while Addis Abeba accuses Khartoum of backing Tigrayan rebels involved in renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia. Both sides deny the allegations against them. Reda, made these allegations during a meeting with UN Special Envoy Guang Cong, where they discussed regional conflicts, particularly in Sudan and Somalia. Getachew urged both Eritrea and Sudan to cease their support for these groups to foster dialogue and prevent further escalation. The accusations come amid rising tensions, marked by reciprocal expulsions of diplomatic staff between Ethiopia and Sudan, as both nations accuse each other of backing insurgents. ethiopia.title: Abiy and Mohamud Meet at COP31 as Somalia-Ethiopia Tensions Simmer Beneath Climate Talks - FTL Somalia
ethiopia.content: Abiy and Mohamud Meet at COP31 as Somalia-Ethiopia Tensions Simmer Beneath Climate Talks - Somali News today Live Home Politics Security Elections More News Premium Economy & Business Education Entertainment & Lifestyle Environment & Climate Health International Relations Technology & Innovation Sports News By Region Nationwide Benadir Galmudug Hirshabelle Jubaland Puntland South West State Somaliland North Eastern State Resources Infographics Downloads Videos FAQ About Somalia Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Home Politics Security Elections More News Premium Economy & Business Education Entertainment & Lifestyle Environment & Climate Health International Relations Technology & Innovation Sports News By Region Nationwide Benadir Galmudug Hirshabelle Jubaland Puntland South West State Somaliland North Eastern State Resources Infographics Downloads Videos FAQ About Somalia Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors Generic selectors Exact matches only Search in title Search in content Post Type Selectors International Relations Nationwide Abiy and Mohamud Meet at COP31 as Somalia-Ethiopia Tensions Simmer Beneath Climate Talks November 11, 2026 5 min read ANTALYA , Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed met with Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on the sidelines of the COP31 Leaders’ Summit in Antalya on Wednesday, in a bilateral encounter that placed the two leaders together for the first time since Somalia’s diplomatic realignment toward Egypt and Algeria deepened tensions with Addis Ababa. In a post on X, Abiy said the two leaders exchanged views on “the current security situation in Somalia and broader regional developments, emphasizing the importance of continued dialogue and cooperation in advancing regional peace and stability.” The statement was notably brief and did not reference any specific agreements or outcomes from the meeting. The encounter comes at a moment of extraordinary complexity in Somalia-Ethiopia relations, one shaped by competing security partnerships, unresolved sovereignty disputes, and the shifting geopolitics of the Red Sea and the Nile. A Relationship Rebuilt, Then Tested Again The Abiy-Mohamud meeting is the latest chapter in a relationship that has oscillated between crisis and dialogue over the past two years. Relations were strained in early 2024 after Ethiopia signed a memorandum of understanding with Somaliland to secure sea access, a move Mogadishu condemned as a violation of its sovereignty, as documented in coverage of the diplomatic crisis . The crisis was defused through Turkish mediation, leading to the Ankara Declaration in December 2024, in which both countries reaffirmed respect for each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. President Mohamud has visited Ethiopia several times since then, including for the inauguration of the Aysha-II Wind Power Project in January 2026 and the 39th African Union Summit in February. In June 2026, the two leaders held talks in Addis Ababa on security, economic ties, and regional stability, as reported in the coverage of the earlier summit . But the relationship has been strained by Somalia’s deepening military partnership with Egypt. Cairo has pledged approximately 1,091 troops to AUSSOM, with its contingent expected to deploy in the Middle Shabelle region. Ethiopia views Egypt’s military presence in Somalia with deep suspicion, seeing it as a strategic threat tied to the broader rivalry over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and Red Sea influence. In September 2026, as Abiy and Mohamud met in Addis Ababa, Egyptian military officials arrived in Mogadishu to establish a base near the Isiley airstrip in Middle Shabelle, a deployment that Somali officials framed as part of the AU mission but that Ethiopian analysts viewed as a direct challenge, as detailed in the analysis of the Egypt factor . The Alamein Factor and the Sovereignty Question The Antalya meeting also follows Somalia’s participation in the Alamein Declaration in October 2026, a four-nation statement by Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia, and Sudan that rejected any recognition of Somaliland and affirmed that Red Sea governance is the exclusive responsibility of littoral states. The declaration also stressed respect for international law on transboundary rivers, a clear reference to Ethiopia’s Nile dam dispute with Egypt and Sudan. For Addis Ababa, Somalia’s alignment with the Alamein bloc is a source of concern. Ethiopia has consistently rejected what it calls “coercive measures” by downstream Nile states and has framed its pursuit of sea access as an existential necessity, as reported in the coverage of Ethiopia’s response to the declaration . Prime Minister Abiy has repeatedly stated that sea access is a matter of survival for Ethiopia’s 130 million people, a position that places him at odds with Mogadishu’s insistence that any arrangement must go through the federal government and not through bilateral deals with Somaliland. The COP31 meeting may have been an opportunity for the two leaders to manage these tensions privately, away from the formal diplomatic channels that have produced public statements and declarations. The brief readout from Abiy’s office suggests a meeting focused on maintaining dialogue rather than announcing breakthroughs. Critical Note The Abiy-Mohamud meeting in Antalya is a welcome sign that the two leaders are still talking. In a region where diplomatic channels can close quickly and decisively, the fact that they met at all is a positive development. The emphasis on “continued dialogue and cooperation” is the right language, even if it is the language of every bilateral readout. But a meeting on the sidelines of a climate summit is not a resolution. The fundamental tensions between Somalia and Ethiopia remain unresolved. Ethiopia’s pursuit of sea access, Somalia’s deepening partnership with Egypt, and the unresolved status of the Somaliland question are not issues that can be settled in a brief encounter at a conference centre in Antalya. They require sustained negotiation, likely with external mediation, and a willingness on both sides to make concessions that neither has shown publicly. The timing is also delicate. Somalia’s relationship with Ethiopia is being reshaped by forces beyond the bilateral relationship, from Egypt’s military deployment to the UAE’s regional strategy to the Red Sea security crisis. The two leaders may have met to manage their differences, but the broader regional dynamics that drive those differences are not within their control. The Antalya meeting was a conversation. Whether it becomes a turning point will depend on what happens after the climate summit ends and the delegations return home. The leaders discussed the security situation in Somalia and regional developments, emphasizing the need for ongoing dialogue and cooperation. However, their brief exchange did not yield any specific agreements. While the meeting is a positive sign of continued communication, the underlying tensions remain unresolved, requiring sustained negotiation and potential external mediation to address the broader regional dynamics influencing their relationship.

ethiopia.title: News - Renewed Fighting in Tigray Pushes Its Fragile Healthcare System Closer to Collapse, Again
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: News - Renewed Fighting in Tigray Pushes Its Fragile Healthcare System Closer to Collapse, Again - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: News - Renewed Fighting in Tigray Pushes Its Fragile Healthcare System Closer to Collapse, Again 11 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia has overwhelmed hospitals, disrupted medical services and deepened an already severe healthcare crisis in Tigray, with medical workers warning that civilians increasingly risk being left without access to emergency treatment, according to a report by National Public Radio (NPR). The report, published on November 10, documents how hospitals in Mekelle, the regional capital, were overwhelmed within days of renewed clashes between Ethiopian federal forces and Tigrayan forces on September 23, marking a further unravelling of the two-year cessation of hostilities agreement. A surgeon at a Mekelle hospital, who spoke anonymously over concerns about repercussions for treating wounded combatants, described seven to eight days of chaos as casualties from gunfire, drone strikes and mortar attacks flooded the emergency department. "It was a mess, it was chaos, and that continued for almost seven, eight days. Without (cell) network, without electricity," the surgeon said. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn "The whole emergency (room) was flooded with war trauma patients. The floors were all filled up, there was no place to step," he added, describing how medical staff treated patients without knowing how many more casualties were arriving or where they were coming from. "We don't know where they're from -- you just go ahead and do whatever you can, you know?" he said. The renewed conflict has compounded longstanding shortages of healthcare workers, medicines, ambulances and medical equipment. Doctors in Tigray have reportedly gone unpaid for months following the federal government's suspension of funding to the region after local leaders were ousted in May. Following late-October drone strikes that killed at least 15 people, including children, World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that the conflict was further undermining healthcare access. "The conflict is pushing an already fragile health system closer to collapse," Tedros said, adding that "as fighting continues, more people are likely to lose access to essential healthcare." He called for civilian protection, saying: "The most courageous choose peace." The current crisis comes against the backdrop of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war, which killed upwards 600,000 people and left much of the region's healthcare infrastructure decimated or only partially operational. Attacks on medical facilities and personnel have also persisted since the November 2022 cessation of hostilities agreement. A 2024 report by Physicians for Human Rights found that 63% of surveyed healthcare workers reported attacks on ambulances, while 57% had witnessed armed takeovers of clinics or hospitals. Lindsey Green, a Physicians for Human Rights researcher focusing on Ethiopia, told NPR that continued attacks were undermining the protection traditionally afforded to healthcare facilities during armed conflicts. "The continual attack against healthcare is eroding the norm of healthcare being a protected part of conflict," she said. Green said armed groups had occupied medical facilities to seize or destroy resources, including equipment and machinery, making healthcare increasingly difficult to access. She linked the pattern to the lack of accountability for violations. A healthcare worker in Tigray, also speaking anonymously, told NPR that more than 100 maternal deaths had been recorded in the region over the past year, attributing them to shortages of medicines, medical personnel and fuel, which had left ambulances non-functional. "They died during delivery because of a lack of medicine, lack of health care providers, a lack of fuel. So the ambulances are not functional," the worker said. The health worker also recalled how medical personnel had been told during the previous war that civilians should be punished for allegedly supporting the TPLF. Ayoda Werede, a California-based physician with Health Professionals for Tigray, said renewed fighting had created opportunities for looting, with unidentified groups stealing medicines, medical equipment and even mattresses from hospital beds. "This was just the opportunistic vacuum space that was created because of this conflict," Ayoda told NPR. The crisis has also been compounded by reductions in international humanitarian assistance, including cuts associated with the dismantling of USAID, while shortages and continued looting have further depleted medical supplies. Many doctors have reportedly left the country. Reflecting on the recurrence of violence and the unresolved consequences of the previous war, the Mekelle surgeon described the crisis as an injury that had never properly healed. "It's an open wound, which was never closed, you know. Left for healing and never healed. I guess now it's infected," he said. "We've lost our sense of being secure. Hospitals in Mekelle have been overwhelmed by casualties from recent clashes between Ethiopian federal forces and Tigrayan fighters, which reignited a two-year cessation of hostilities. Medical staff report chaotic conditions, with emergency rooms flooded and resources stretched thin. The conflict has exacerbated existing shortages of healthcare workers, medicines, and ambulances, with many doctors going unpaid for months. Attacks on medical facilities have persisted, with reports of looting and armed takeovers, complicating the delivery of essential services. A healthcare worker noted over 100 maternal deaths in the past year due to a lack of resources. The situation reflects a deepening crisis, with the region's healthcare infrastructure still reeling from the devastating Tigray war of 2020-2022.

ethiopia.title: Tanzanian Delegation Interested in Ethiopia's Agricultural Commodity Standards Practice
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Tanzanian Delegation Interested in Ethiopia's Agricultural Commodity Standards Practice - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Tanzanian Delegation Interested in Ethiopia's Agricultural Commodity Standards Practice 10 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Tanzania's Capital Markets Tribunal Chairperson, Ntemi Nimilwa Kilekamajenga, has expressed interest in Ethiopia's experience in ensuring that agricultural commodities meet international market standards, citing the Ethiopian Commodity Exchange's quality assessment practices and specialized academy as valuable institutional lessons. The Tanzanian delegation head told ENA that the delegation was particularly impressed by the Commodity Exchange's extensive range of traded agricultural products and the academy which plays an important role in ensuring the quality of agricultural commodities destined for export. He noted that Ethiopia trades a wider range of agricultural products than Tanzania, citing maize, which is not currently among the commodities traded through Tanzania's commodity exchange, as one example. The delegation head identified the Ethiopian experience as an important lesson, particularly the need to consider expanding the range of agricultural products traded through Tanzania's commodity exchange. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Kilekamajenga said the academy established by the Ethiopian Commodity Exchange was a notable practice that a Tanzanian commodity exchange staff should visit Ethiopia and learn how the institution ensures exported agricultural products meet internationally required quality standards. He stated that Tanzania's Ministry of Finance accompanying the delegation had also developed an interest in exploring ways to facilitate such a learning visit upon their return. The delegation also gained firsthand insight into how the exchange applies its quality assurance system, particularly in assessing coffee destined for international markets, Eliad E. Mndeme, a Tanzanian lawyer and member of the delegation, said. He said the delegation was taken through the coffee assessment process, which involves evaluating its taste, aroma and preparation; and also had an opportunity to participate in testing the coffee. Mndeme said the quality assurance mechanism gives international buyers confidence that coffee traded through the exchange meets the required standards. He also highlighted the financial benefits of the system, explaining that farmers who obtain quality certificates from the exchange can use them to secure bank loans as the certificates serve as tradable. Overall, the delegation aims to enhance Tanzania's agricultural commodity exchange by adopting successful practices from Ethiopia.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Pledges Inclusive COP32 Process, Puts LDC Priorities At Center of Climate Agenda
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia Pledges Inclusive COP32 Process, Puts LDC Priorities At Center of Climate Agenda - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia Pledges Inclusive COP32 Process, Puts LDC Priorities At Center of Climate Agenda 10 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Ethiopia reaffirmed its commitment to advancing the climate priorities of Least Developed Countries (LDCs), pledging an inclusive, transparent and collaborative process as it prepares to host the 32nd United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP32) in Addis Ababa in November 2027. Foreign Affairs Minister and COP32 President-Designate Gedion Timothewos reaffirmed the commitment during talks with LDC Group Chair Ambassador Adão Soares Barbosa of Timor-Leste at the Ethiopia Pavilion on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. Gedion underscored the importance of close consultation and strong partnerships to ensure that the priorities, interests and perspectives of LDCs remain central to COP32 preparations and deliberations. He stressed that Ethiopia intends to work closely with the LDC Group and other international partners to build consensus and advance climate outcomes that reflect the shared aspirations of vulnerable countries. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines The Minister also emphasized that a successful COP31 would provide a critical foundation for COP32, helping sustain momentum in global climate negotiations and deliver meaningful progress on collective climate action. Ethiopia is using its participation in COP31 to strengthen international partnerships, support constructive negotiations and build momentum for its upcoming presidency. Speaking on Monday, Gedion said Ethiopia's foremost priority at the Antalya conference is to contribute to a successful negotiation process that will lay a strong foundation for more effective outcomes at COP32. To this end, Ethiopia will work closely with the Turkish and Australian COP31 presidencies to support ongoing negotiations and facilitate a smooth and constructive transition to the next climate conference. Mobilizing international partnerships and building a shared understanding of Ethiopia's COP32 vision are also central to the country's engagement, he said, adding that the government is seeking to exchange perspectives, identify common interests and establish areas of cooperation with potential partners. Ethiopia also aims to use the global climate gathering to generate wider international interest in COP32 and encourage broad participation in the Addis Ababa summit. Gedion noted that the Ethiopia Pavilion is serving as a platform for dialogue, partnership-building and showcasing the country's climate initiatives, while offering international participants an early glimpse of Ethiopia's preparations and hospitality as the next COP host. somalia.title: Somalia repatriates 170 stranded migrants from Libya with EU support - Hiiraan Online
somalia.content: Somalia repatriates 170 stranded migrants from Libya with EU support - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME NEWS Somalia repatriates 170 stranded migrants from Libya with EU support Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Wednesday November 11, 2026 Mogadishu (HOL) — Somali federal government welcomed home 170 migrants repatriated from Libya on Tuesday through a European Union-supported voluntary return program, allowing them to reunite with their families after months stranded in the North African country. The operation was carried out in coordination with the federal government and supported by the European Union in Somalia through the Voluntary Humanitarian Return program, which assists vulnerable migrants seeking to return safely to their home countries. The returnees included children and young adults who had endured difficult conditions during irregular migration journeys and while stranded in Libya. advertisements Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation Minister Ali Yusuf Ali Hoosh said the migrants had faced serious humanitarian challenges, including exploitation by human traffickers and harsh conditions in detention facilities. Some of the returnees were experiencing health problems following their experiences in Libya, according to officials involved in the operation. “The government and its partners had prepared assistance programs to help the returning migrants rebuild their lives in Somalia,” Hoosh said. The planned support includes medical care, employment opportunities and other reintegration services aimed at helping returnees recover and become economically self-sufficient. The European Union in Somalia described the return as safe, voluntary and dignified, emphasizing the importance of protecting migrants from trafficking and abuse while helping them reunite with their families. The EU-supported program aims to provide vulnerable migrants with an opportunity to return home and rebuild their lives after experiencing hardship abroad. Hoosh urged Somali youth to avoid dangerous irregular migration routes, warning that journeys across deserts and the Mediterranean Sea expose migrants to human trafficking, exploitation, detention and other life-threatening risks. He also encouraged the returnees not to lose hope and to take advantage of opportunities available in Somalia. The reception operation involved several Somali government agencies, including the Immigration and Citizenship Agency, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation and the Somali Police Force, alongside international partners supporting the return program. Libya has long served as a major transit point for migrants attempting to reach Europe through the Mediterranean Sea, including Somalis seeking better economic opportunities or fleeing insecurity. Migrants traveling through Libya frequently face risks including arbitrary detention, exploitation by trafficking networks and dangerous sea crossings. The latest return operation forms part of continuing efforts by the Somali government and international partners to assist vulnerable citizens stranded abroad and support their voluntary return and reintegration into their communities. somalia.title: Somalia: Disease outbreaks surge after floods, straining health services - Africa.com
somalia.content: Somalia: Disease outbreaks surge after floods, straining health services | africa.com africa.com Support Us Subscribe to Our Newsletter African Nations Arts, Culture & Society Doing Business in Africa Engage & Learn Features & Opinion What's Happening Knowledge Partners Latest News More African Nations Arts, Culture & Society Doing Business in Africa Engage & Learn Features & Opinion What's Happening Knowledge Partners Latest News More Home / APO / Somalia Disease Outbreaks Surge After Floods Straining Health Services ← APO Group / Africa Newsroom Press release APO Group · 11 November 2026 Somalia: Disease outbreaks surge after floods, straining health services OCHA is sounding the alarm over a surge in disease outbreaks following recent floods in the region of Mudug in Somalia’s north, where suspected cholera and acute watery diarrhoea cases are rising rapidly. Health authorities have confirmed five cholera cases, including one death, in eastern Gaalkacyo, the capital of Mudug region. Since the start of the year, more than 5,800 acute watery diarrhoea cases have been reported across the region, including more than 1,900 in the last two months. Authorities attribute the outbreak primarily to contaminated water sources and overflowing latrines following the floods. Meanwhile, a bit further south in Hirshabelle State, health authorities have reported more than 1,800 suspected measles cases and 102 suspected diphtheria cases since January. Humanitarian partners working in health say that low immunization coverage, limited access to health services and seasonal rains could fuel the spread of disease. The World Health Organization and the UN’s partners are stepping up efforts to respond, working closely with local health authorities. Mobile medical teams and emergency supplies are being deployed, and disease surveillance is being strengthened. Partners are also expanding water quality testing and treatment, malaria prevention measures and hygiene campaigns, while preparing to increase capacity to treat patients. But health facilities are struggling to cope due to overcrowding and shortages of essential supplies. More funding is urgently needed to contain these outbreaks and save lives. Less than 40 per cent of the $852 million needed for the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan has been received so far, with less than one-third of health funding requirements met. somalia.summary: Following severe flooding in Somalia's Mudug region, health services are under significant strain due to a surge in disease outbreaks. The UN's Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports rising cases of suspected cholera and acute watery diarrhoea, with five confirmed cholera cases, including one fatality, in Gaalkacyo. Since January, over 5,800 acute watery diarrhoea cases have been documented, exacerbated by contaminated water and overflowing latrines. Additionally, Hirshabelle State has seen more than 1,800 suspected measles cases and 102 suspected diphtheria cases. Contributing factors include low immunization rates and limited healthcare access. In response, the World Health Organization and humanitarian partners are deploying mobile medical teams and enhancing disease surveillance, but health facilities are overwhelmed and under-resourced. Urgent funding is needed, as less than 40% of the required $852 million for the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan has been secured, with health funding falling short of one-third of its target.

somalia.title: Somalia: Disease outbreaks surge after floods | Health services now seriously strained - The Tanzania Times
somalia.content: Somalia: Diseases break out after floods | Health Services strained The Tanzania Times - News from Tanzania, Africa, World, Breaking News, Weather, Environment and Climate Change National Africa Finance Climate Technology Lifestyle Forex Africa Health Somalia: Disease outbreaks surge after floods | Health services now seriously strained Tanzania Times Nov 11, 2026 Share The Northern Somalia region is submerged under floods. But floods are only part of the problem. The environmental disaster is also yielding serious diseases that are affecting people. In connection with that, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) is now sounding the alarm over a surge in disease outbreaks following recent floods in the region of Mudug in Somalia’s north, where suspected cholera and acute watery diarrhea cases are rising rapidly. Health authorities have so far confirmed five cholera cases, including one death, in Eastern Gaalkacyo, the capital of Mudug region. Since the start of the year, more than 5,800 acute watery diarrhea cases have been reported across the Northern Sudan’s region, including more than 1,900 recorded in the last two months. Authorities in the area attribute the outbreak primarily to contaminated water sources and overflowing pit latrines following the floods. Meanwhile, a bit further south in Hirshabelle State, health authorities have reported more than 1,800 suspected measles cases and 102 suspected diphtheria cases since January. Humanitarian partners working in health say that low immunization coverage, limited access to health services and seasonal rains could fuel the spread of disease. The World Health Organization (WHO) and the United Nations (UN) partners are stepping up efforts to respond, working closely with local health authorities. Mobile medical teams and emergency supplies are being deployed, and disease surveillance is being strengthened. Partners are also expanding water quality testing and treatment, malaria prevention measures and hygiene campaigns, while preparing to increase capacity to treat patients. But health facilities happen to be also struggling to cope with the influx due to overcrowding and shortages of essential supplies. More funding is urgently needed to contain these outbreaks and save lives. Less than 40 percent of the US$ 852 million needed for the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan has been received so far, with less than one-third of health funding requirements met. Somalia has been suffering from severe flooding in 2026. The El-Nino driven rains have led to rising water levels in the country affecting more than 175,000 people. need six points: Bjorkegren demands focus as Black Stars prepare for Somalia Qualifiers 4 hours ago Advertisement Black Stars head coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren says Ghana must take six points from the double-header against Somalia, starting with Thursday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, insisting the team must respect the opposition but believe in its own quality to deliver a win in front of the Takoradi crowd. Speaking to the press in Takoradi on Wednesday ahead of the first of the two games, Bjorkegren reflected on his first days in charge, what he brings to the team, his message to the players, the return of key players, and the impact of playing in front of the home fans. Here is what he had to say: On what he’s been up to since appointment I have been doing my best, I must say. I've been around a little bit in Europe and watched some players, I've tried to connect with more or less all of the players by phone. And now that we have been here in Ghana, we have been trying to do our best with the two trainings that we have had so far. We will have another one today. There have been some meetings, of course, where we have discussed how we want to be tomorrow, how we want to play, how we want to create chances, how we want to go forward, score goals, and the most important, how we want to win this game tomorrow. On what he brings to the team as a coach No, to be honest, it's not about me. Some people maybe think about it that way, but I don't think it is. For me, it's all about doing the best for the players. Of course, my job is also to support them, to let them know that I'm there, to give them a game plan that is not too difficult, but in the same way that, like I said, we have been talking about where we think that we can create chances from when it comes to the opponent, in this case, Somalia. We know that we have so many quality players in the team, so as long as we see them with good energy, good fighting spirit, team spirit and everything like that, I'm not that worried about the game. On message to players about the two matches Yeah, it's super clear. It's not a secret that we need six points, but we need to take it. It's old school, but we need to take the game tomorrow to start with. It will not be easy. We saw it when Somalia, for example, played against Ivory Coast. They were really close to take a point there. They had a great fighting spirit. They make it difficult for the opponent, so we need to respect them, but in the same way, believing in ourselves. On having Kudus , Partey, Jordan, Salisu and other key players back in the team This is the first camp as a head coach I'm doing with the Black Stars, but so far they have been great, I would say. And of course, when it comes to good, experienced players, in a little bit difficult situation where we are right now, I think it can be helpful. Of course, a little bit of pressure when it comes to performing good results, but the players you talked about, they are there and they are used to delivering under pressure. So I think, again, I'm coming back to, I think the most important thing for them will be to feel that they have the freedom to do what they can and then just work hard together as a group. On playing in front of the Takoradi crowd and its impact Yeah, we have talked a little bit about it. Not so much, of course, the focus has been on ourselves and those kinds of things. But what I said is that we had a great experience here. We really enjoyed it when we were here last time. We had a great support. So together with the fans, it's going to be a great day tomorrow. So just enjoy the day tomorrow, that's all. On what he brings on board A win. I mean, that's simple like that, what we need. But I keep saying the same thing. It's not just about me. There is not something specific I need to do more than let the guys know that they are so good. So as long as they are doing what they can do, what they are doing in the club teams and just support each other on the pitch tomorrow, if we can keep a good energy out there, then I'm pretty sure that we're going to have a good result. Business Insider Edition United States International Deutschland & Österreich España Japan México Nederland Polska ADVERTISEMENT BI Africa > local > markets China calls US-backed Israel its friend despite earlier warnings over its recognition of Somaliland and military strikes on Iran Olamilekan Okebiorun 11 November 2026 08:00 PM In an unexpected diplomatic turn, China has described Israel as a friend and important partner, months after condemning its military strikes on Iran and strongly opposing its recognition of Somaliland, two issues that have placed Beijing at odds with the Jewish state. China and Saudi Arabia opposed Israel’s recognition of Somaliland in December 2025, citing Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Photo credit: BIA Beijing strongly opposed Israel's recognition of Somaliland, aligning with Somalia and condemning foreign interference. Despite condemning US-Israeli strikes on Iran, China emphasized its neutrality and continued cooperation with both Israel and Iran. China continues to grow economic ties with Israel, showing a willingness to prioritize economic interests over political disagreements. ADVERTISEMENT Read Also markets Russia bows out of attempt to replace US dollar with Chinese yuan after years of promoting currency alternatives among its BRICS friends markets As Israel advances embassy plans in a breakaway nation despite warnings from China and other global powers, the US reveals why it left a key airbase in Somalia after 14 years markets After France evacuated its ex-president, Africa’s new military government faces a warning from the world's most powerful military over Russian involvement The remarks came from Chinese Ambassador to Israel Xiao Junzheng in an interview with JNS, as Beijing finds itself navigating tensions between its close partner Iran and Israel, a key US ally. "Israel is a friend of China and an important partner," Xiao declared, in comments that contrast with Beijing's earlier diplomatic warnings and its continued opposition to Israel's activities in the Horn of Africa. China calls Israel a friend after opposing its Somaliland recognition ADVERTISEMENT China's latest friendly remarks follow a major diplomatic dispute over Africa, after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu recognised Somaliland as an independent state on December 26, 2025, drawing condemnation from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt and several other countries. Three days later, China's Foreign Ministry formally rejected the move, warning against foreign interference in Somalia's internal affairs and reaffirming its support for Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity. "China expresses grave concern over Israel’s recognition of Somaliland and is firmly against it," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian declared during a press briefing in Beijing. The dispute continued in October 2026, when Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Djibouti's Foreign Minister Abdoulkader Houssein Omar reaffirmed their opposition to Somaliland's recognition during talks in Beijing, as Israel advanced efforts to establish an embassy in Hargeisa. "Both sides firmly support Somalia in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity, oppose any attempt to gain ‘diplomatic recognition’ for Somaliland," the two governments said in a joint statement. ADVERTISEMENT The issue holds strategic importance for China, which operates its first overseas military base in Djibouti, near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and Somaliland, which declared independence from Somalia in 1991. Despite these disagreements, Xiao's latest remarks show Beijing's willingness to maintain close economic and diplomatic ties with Israel, even as the two countries remain divided over regional issues. China condemns Iran strikes but praises its support for Israel during war China's position becomes more striking when viewed alongside its relationship with Iran, another longstanding diplomatic and economic partner. In March 2026, Beijing strongly condemned the US-Israeli military strikes on Iran, arguing that the attacks violated international law and calling for an immediate end to hostilities. ADVERTISEMENT "The U.S.-Israeli strikes against Iran have no UN Security Council authorization and violate international law," China's Foreign Ministry declared. However, despite Beijing's opposition to the strikes and its longstanding ties with Tehran, Xiao stressed that China was not directly involved in the confrontation. "We are not a party to the conflict between the U.S., Israel and Iran," he told JNS. The ambassador then offered a different perspective on China's relationship with Israel, defending Chinese investments in the country's ports, railways and other infrastructure despite longstanding Israeli security concerns. "I must remind our Israeli friends that cooperation between us serves the interests of both sides," Xiao said. "It is also critical for Israel, especially during wartime." ADVERTISEMENT He pointed to the continued operation of Chinese-backed infrastructure during missile and drone attacks as evidence of the value of Beijing's investments. "When this country was under threat from missiles and drones, those infrastructure projects maintained operation and provided significant assistance to the Israeli government and people," he added. somalia.summary: In a surprising diplomatic shift, China has labeled Israel as a "friend" and "important partner," despite previously condemning Israel's military actions against Iran and its recognition of Somaliland. This change comes after months of tension, particularly following Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's recognition of Somaliland in December 2025, which China opposed, citing Somalia's sovereignty. Chinese Ambassador to Israel, Xiao Junzheng, emphasized China's neutrality in the Israel-Iran conflict while highlighting ongoing economic cooperation, including investments in Israeli infrastructure. Despite condemning US-Israeli strikes on Iran, China appears willing to prioritize economic interests over political disagreements. The remarks reflect China's complex diplomatic balancing act, as it navigates relationships with both Israel and Iran while maintaining its stance on issues of sovereignty in the Horn of Africa. This development underscores China's strategic interests in the region, particularly given its military base in Djibouti, near Somaliland.

Ghana Football Association Interim Black Stars head coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren says Ghana are targeting maximum points from their two matches against Somalia as they look to revive their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying campaign. Ghana host Somalia at the Essipong Stadium in the first of the two encounters before travelling for the return fixture, with the Black Stars aware that anything less than two wins would further complicate their chances of reaching the tournament. Advertisement Advertisement The four-time African champions have endured a difficult start to the qualifiers, losing their opening two matches against Ivory Coast and Gambia . Those results have left Ghana under pressure in Group C and with little room for further setbacks. Group C standings for 2027 AFCON qualifiers Flahscore Speaking ahead of the first meeting, Bjorkegren acknowledged the importance of collecting all six points but insisted that Ghana would not underestimate their opponents. “It’s not a secret that we need all six points, but we need to respect Somalia, ” he said. The interim coach is confident Ghana have the quality to produce the performances required, stressing the need for an attacking approach and greater efficiency in front of goal. “We have the potential to play good football and create chances to win the game against Somalia. “We want to play. We want to create chances. We want to move forward. We want to score goals,” he added. Bjorkegren is stepping into the role following the departure of Carlos Queiroz, who was appointed to lead Ghana after the team's disappointing 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign but left his position after the opening two AFCON qualifying defeats. The Ghana Football Association has since turned to the Black Queens coach to take temporary charge of the senior men's team while the search for a substantive head coach continues. Thomas-Asante welcomes Takoradi support Brandon Thomas-Asante also expressed his excitement about Ghana playing the Somalia fixture in Takoradi, with the Black Stars set to host the match at the Essipong Stadium. The forward said the welcome the team received from supporters had created a positive atmosphere around the camp. “It’s a real blessing because even when we got off the bus for training, you could feel the atmosphere. There’s an energy. It’s a change. It’s positive,” Thomas-Asante said. “We also recognise that there’s support all across the country. To be able to have these two games here is a blessing.” Ghana will hope to turn that support into a positive result as they seek to get their qualifying campaign back on track. Here is how the Black Stars could line up at the Essipong Sports Stadium. Advertisement Black Stars of Ghana are expected to make several changes as they prepare to face Somalia in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON ) qualifying campaign, with caretaker coach Kim Lars looking to guide the team to victory. Advertisement Advertisement The four-time African champions will take on the Ocean Stars at the Essipong Sports Stadium on Thursday, with kick-off scheduled for 3:00 pm GMT. Kim Lars, who has taken charge of the national team in a caretaker capacity, will be hoping to turn Ghana’s fortunes around after a disappointing start to the qualifiers, which has seen the Black Stars fail to secure a win in their opening two matches. Ghana began their qualifying campaign with a 2-4 defeat against Gambia under former coach Carlos Queiroz before suffering another setback in a 0-2 loss to Côte d’Ivoire. With the team desperate to get its campaign back on track, attention will now turn to the possible starting XI Kim Lars could select for Thursday’s encounter. Advertisement Advertisement Here is Pulse Ghana ’s predicted Black Stars line-up against Somalia. Goalkeeper Benjamin Asare Black Stars goalkeeper Benjamin Asare Hearts of Oak goalkeeper Benjamin Asare is expected to retain his place between the posts following his impressive performances in the Ghana Premier League. Advertisement Advertisement After nine league matches, the shot-stopper has recorded seven clean sheets, conceding goals in only two games. His consistency and current form make him a strong candidate to start against Somalia, with Kim Lars likely to favor continuity by keeping him in goal for the home fixture. Defenders Gideon MENSAH of Ghana during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Group L match between England and Ghana at Boston Stadium on June 23, 2026 in Boston, United States. Photo via IMAGO Jonas Adjetey, Jerome Opoku, Gideon Mensah, and Alidu Seidu Advertisement Advertisement Jonas Adjetey is expected to partner with Jerome Opoku in central defense as Ghana looks to establish stability at the back. Gideon Mensah is tipped to occupy the left-back position, while Alidu Seidu is expected to complete the defensive line-up at right-back. The defensive quartet will have the responsibility of keeping Somalia's attackers at bay while providing support during Ghana's attacking transitions. Midfielders Thomas Partey Thomas Partey, Caleb Yirenkyi, and Daniel Kofi-Kyereh Thomas Partey is expected to anchor Ghana's midfield, using his experience and passing ability to control the tempo of the game. The midfielder will be tasked with distributing possession, breaking up opposition attacks, and helping the Black Stars move forward in search of goals. He could be joined by Caleb Yirenkyi and Daniel Kofi-Kyereh, who are expected to provide energy, creativity, and additional support in the middle of the park. Advertisement Advertisement The three-man midfield could play a crucial role in helping Ghana dominate possession and create opportunities for the attacking players. Attackers Jordan Ayew | Photo via Getty Images Jordan Ayew, Mohammed Kudus, and Prince Adu Kwabena Captain Jordan Ayew is expected to feature in the attacking line-up, bringing his experience and leadership to the team. Advertisement Advertisement Mohammed Kudus could operate behind the main striker, using his creativity, pace, and ability to take on defenders to unlock Somalia's defense. Prince Adu Kwabena is tipped to lead the attack as the central forward, with the responsibility of converting the opportunities created by his teammates. The combination of Ayew, Kudus, and Adu Kwabena could provide Ghana with the attacking threat needed to secure all three points. football.title: باللجوء للمحكمة الرياضية.. أزمة سحب لقب الدوري السوداني من المريخ تتصاعد - متن نيوز
football.content: زمة سحب لقب الدوري السوداني من المريخ تتصاعد الخميس 12 نوفمبر 2026 facebook twitter youtube instagram whatsapp rss feed احدث الاخبار تلفزيون متن الرياضة السياسة الاقتصاد تقارير وتحقيقات الدراسات والابحاث باللجوء للمحكمة الرياضية.. أزمة سحب لقب الدوري السوداني من المريخ تتصاعد المريخ السوداني الأربعاء 11/نوفمبر/2026 - 06:03 م 11/11/2026 6:03:24 PM الرياضة شارك طباعة أكد نادي المريخ السوداني، على رفضه القاطع لقرار لجنة الاستئناف المتعلق بشأن لقب الدوري للموسم الماضي، بعد قبول اللجنة لطلب الفحص من الهلال. وأعلن نادي الهلال مساء أمس الثلاثاء، حصوله على لقب الدوري السوداني الموسم الماضي، بقرار رسمي صادر من قبل لجنة الاستئناف في الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم. وشدد المريخ السوداني في بيانه الرسمي الذي أصدره عبر صفحاته الرسمية، على رفضه القاطع لقرار لجنة الاستئنافات، مؤكدًا على تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية "كاس". وجاء بيان المريخ السوداني كالتالي: "يعلن نادي المريخ الرياضي رفضه القاطع لقرار لجنة الاستئنافات المشكلة حديثًا، والقاضي بقبول طلب الفحص المقدم من النادي الآخر، ونقض القرار السابق الذي قضى بأحقية المريخ في لقب بطولة الدوري الممتاز، وبذلك يؤكد تمسكه بكافة حقوقه ومكتسباته، ورفضه لأي إجراءات تنتقص منها". وواصل في بيانه الرسمي: "ويثير القرار استغراب المجلس، لا سيما أن لجنة الاستئنافات السابقة لم تكتفِ بإصدار قرارها لصالح المريخ، بل أشادت في حيثياته بالاستئناف الذي تقدم به النادي، وأثبتت ذلك صراحة في مضابطها، وهو الأمر الذي قاد الاتحاد السوداني إلى إجراء تعديلات على لائحة أوضاع اللاعبين استنادًا إلى ما انتهت إليه اللجنة للقضية، الأمر الذي يجعل العدول عن ذلك القرار موضع تساؤل قانوني". وأردف في البيان الرسمي: "وتزداد علامات الاستفهام حول القرار الأخير، في ظل تلقي النادي إخطارًا رسميًا من الاتحاد يفيد بانتقال القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية (CAS)، بناءً على الشكوى المقدمة من النادي الآخر بالرقم A/12688. وهو ما يطرح تساؤلات جوهرية حول الأساس القانوني والإجرائي لإعادة النظر في القضية أمام لجنة الاستئنافات، بعد إخطار الأطراف بانتقال النزاع إلى المحكمة الدولية". واستكمل المريخ في بيانه: "وبناءً على كل ذلك وعلى ضوء القرار الأخير حسم مجلس إدارة نادي المريخ أمره وقرر تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية (CAS)، والمضي في كافة الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة، مستندًا إلى خبرات النادي وتجاربه السابقة أمام المحكمة، ومستعينًا بالكفاءات القانونية المتخصصة، دفاعًا عن حقه في البطولة حتى صدور القرار النهائي". وأردف النادي السوداني في بيانه: "وفي هذا الصدد يوجه المجلس وجماهير النادي ورموزه ونجومه وإعلامه وكافة قطاعاته رسالة واضحة إلى الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم، بأن المريخ نادٍ جماهيري وقيادي، له تاريخه ومكانته وقاعدته الممتدة داخل السودان وخارجه، لذلك لن يقبل المساس بحقوقه أو الانتقاص من مقدراته". واستكمل: "وعلى الاتحاد الالتزام بمسؤولياته في إدارة المنافسة بعدالة وأخلاق وحياد، إضافة إلى تطبيق اللوائح دون تمييز أو انتقائية، ونعيد التأكيد بأقوى العبارات أن المريخ لن يقف مكتوف الأيدي أمام أي إجراءات تمس حقوقه، ولن يقبل فرض الأمر الواقع عليه أو العبث بمكتسباته، وسيواجه ذلك بكل الوسائل القانونية والمؤسسية المتاحة". واختتم النادي بيانه: "وإلى جماهير المريخ الوفية، يؤكد المجلس أن حقوق النادي ليست محل مساومة أو تفريط، وأنه ماضٍ في طريق القانون حتى النهاية، وأنتم من خلفنا سندًا والعهد بيننا ألا تراجع إطلاقًا". وقد حسم الدوري السوداني في الموسم الماضي، بشكل مثير للجدل، حيث توج المريخ باللقب رغم فوز الهلال بهدف نظيف في الجولة الأخيرة من البطولة، وجاء ذلك بعد قبول استئناف المريخ ضد قرار لجنة المسابقات بشأن قانونية مشاركة عدد من لاعبي الهلال خلال مباراة القمة بين الفريقين. شارك المريخ السوداني الهلال لجنة الاستئناف نادي المريخ الدوري السوداني الأكثر مشاهدة دي لا فوينتي يدافع عن استبعاد لامين يامال من منتخب إسبانيا.. ويكشف تفاصيل إصابته وسط منافسة أوروبية.. تطورات مستقبل إندريك في ريال مدريد الإصابة football.summary: تتصاعد أزمة سحب لقب الدوري السوداني من نادي المريخ بعد قرار لجنة الاستئناف بقبول طلب نادي الهلال للفحص، مما أدى إلى إعلان الهلال فوزه باللقب. نادي المريخ، في بيان رسمي، أعرب عن رفضه القاطع لهذا القرار وأكد عزمه تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية (CAS). وأشار المريخ إلى أن القرار الأخير يثير تساؤلات قانونية، خاصة بعد أن أشادت اللجنة السابقة بقرارها لصالحه. كما أكد النادي أنه لن يقبل أي إجراءات تمس حقوقه، مشددًا على أهمية إدارة المنافسة بعدالة وحياد. المريخ يعتزم اتخاذ كافة الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة للدفاع عن حقه في البطولة، مع التأكيد على دعم جماهيره. الدوري السوداني شهد جدلًا كبيرًا حول لقبه، حيث توج المريخ رغم فوز الهلال في الجولة الأخيرة، بعد قبول استئناف المريخ بشأن قانونية مشاركة بعض لاعبي الهلال.

football.title: المريخ السوداني يعلن التصعيد إلى المحكمة الرياضية بعد سحب لقب الدوري - Masrawy
football.content: المريخ السوداني يصعّد أزمة لقب الدوري إلى المحكمة الرياضية الرئيسية رياضة رياضة عالمية المريخ السوداني يعلن التصعيد إلى المحكمة الرياضية بعد سحب لقب الدوري 12:48 م الأربعاء 11 نوفمبر 2026 فريق المريخ السوداني أعلن نادي المريخ السوداني رفضه القاطع لقرار لجنة الاستئنافات بالاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم، بشأن سحب لقب الدوري الممتاز للموسم الماضي ومنحه لمنافسه الهلال، مؤكدًا عزمه تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية «كاس» (CAS). إعلان وكانت لجنة الاستئنافات قد أصدرت قرارًا بقبول طلب الفحص المقدم من نادي الهلال، ونقض القرار السابق الذي منح المريخ أحقية التتويج بلقب الدوري، ليعلن الهلال مساء أمس الثلاثاء حصوله رسميًا على البطولة. وتعود تفاصيل الأزمة إلى الجولة الأخيرة من منافسات الدوري السوداني الموسم الماضي، عندما حقق الهلال الفوز على المريخ بهدف دون مقابل، إلا أن الأخير تُوّج باللقب بعد قبول استئنافه ضد قرار لجنة المسابقات بشأن قانونية مشاركة عدد من لاعبي الهلال في مباراة القمة بين الفريقين. المريخ يتمسك بالتصعيد إلى المحكمة الرياضية وأكد مجلس إدارة المريخ، في بيان رسمي نشره عبر منصاته، رفضه قرار لجنة الاستئنافات، مشددًا على تمسكه بكافة حقوقه ومكتسباته، واعتباره القرار الأخير محل تساؤلات قانونية وإجرائية. وأشار النادي إلى أن لجنة الاستئنافات السابقة سبق أن أصدرت قرارًا لصالحه، بل أشادت في حيثياتها بالاستئناف الذي تقدم به، وهو ما دفع الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم إلى إجراء تعديلات على لائحة أوضاع اللاعبين استنادًا إلى ما انتهت إليه اللجنة في القضية. وأضاف البيان أن علامات الاستفهام تتزايد بشأن القرار الجديد، خاصة بعدما تلقى النادي إخطارًا رسميًا من الاتحاد السوداني يفيد بانتقال النزاع إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية، بناءً على الشكوى المقدمة من الهلال، والمسجلة تحت الرقم A/12688. وأوضح المريخ أن هذا الإجراء يثير تساؤلات بشأن الأساس القانوني لإعادة فتح القضية أمام لجنة الاستئنافات، بعد إخطار الأطراف بانتقال النزاع إلى المحكمة الرياضية الدولية. المريخ: لن نفرط في حقوق النادي وشدد مجلس إدارة النادي على اتخاذ قرار نهائي بتصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية، والمضي في جميع الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة، بالاستعانة بخبرات قانونية متخصصة، للدفاع عن أحقية الفريق في اللقب حتى صدور الحكم النهائي. كما وجّه المجلس رسالة إلى الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم، مطالبًا إياه بالالتزام بمسؤولياته في إدارة المسابقات وفق مبادئ العدالة والحياد، وتطبيق اللوائح دون تمييز أو انتقائية. واختتم المريخ بيانه بالتأكيد على أن حقوق النادي ليست محل مساومة أو تفريط، وأنه سيواصل اتخاذ المسارات القانونية والمؤسسية المتاحة للدفاع عن موقفه، مع توجيه رسالة طمأنة إلى جماهيره بأن المجلس متمسك بالقضية حتى النهاية. المريخ السوداني الهلال الدوري السوداني إعلان الأخبار المتعلقة شباب أهلي دبي يعلن جاهزيته لمواجهة الهلال السعودي في دوري أبطال النخبة الهلال يهزم الفتح بثنائية ويستعيد صدارة دوري روشن السعودي إعلان انتصارات مثيرة للهلال والنصر والأهلي والاتحاد في دوري روشن المريخ السوداني يكشف حقيقة تحمله تكاليف ملاعب الزمالك في رواندا الرئيسية أخبار رياضة صور وفيديوهات لايف ستايل فنون سيارات إسلاميات 2026 جميع الحقوق محفوظة لدى

الهلال، وإلغاء القرار السابق الذي منح المريخ أحقية التتويج بالبطولة. وكان نادي الهلال السوداني قد أعلن مساء أمس الثلاثاء حصوله رسميًا على لقب الدوري الممتاز للموسم الماضي، بعد صدور قرار من لجنة الاستئنافات بالاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم، يقضي بقبول طلب الفحص المقدم من النادي. وفي المقابل، أصدر مجلس إدارة المريخ بيانًا رسميًا عبر منصاته المختلفة، أكد خلاله رفضه القاطع للقرار الأخير، مشددًا على تمسكه بحقه في لقب البطولة، واتخاذه قرارًا باللجوء إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية «CAS» لمواصلة المعركة القانونية. وأوضح النادي في بيانه أن قرار لجنة الاستئنافات الجديدة تضمن قبول طلب الفحص المقدم من الهلال، وإلغاء الحكم السابق الذي أقر بأحقية المريخ في التتويج بلقب الدوري الممتاز، مؤكدًا أن مجلس الإدارة لن يتنازل عن حقوق النادي أو أي من مكتسباته. وأشار المريخ إلى أن موقفه يستند إلى ما صدر عن لجنة الاستئنافات السابقة، التي أصدرت قرارًا لصالحه، وأشادت في حيثيات حكمها بالاستئناف الذي تقدم به النادي، وهو ما تم إثباته في محاضرها الرسمية، لافتًا إلى أن الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم أجرى تعديلات على لائحة أوضاع اللاعبين استنادًا إلى ما انتهت إليه اللجنة في القضية، الأمر الذي يضع قرار التراجع عن الحكم السابق أمام العديد من التساؤلات القانونية. وأضاف البيان أن علامات الاستفهام تتزايد بشأن القرار الأخير، خاصة أن النادي سبق أن تلقى إخطارًا رسميًا من الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم يفيد بإحالة النزاع إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية، بناءً على الشكوى المقدمة من الهلال تحت رقم A/12688، وهو ما يثير تساؤلات حول المبررات القانونية والإجرائية التي استندت إليها لجنة الاستئنافات في إعادة فتح الملف، رغم إخطار الأطراف بانتقال القضية إلى المحكمة الدولية. وأكد مجلس إدارة المريخ أنه حسم موقفه باللجوء إلى المحكمة الرياضية الدولية «كاس»، مع اتخاذ جميع الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة، والاستعانة بمجموعة من المتخصصين في القضايا الرياضية، مستندًا إلى خبرات النادي السابقة في التعامل مع المحكمة، بهدف الحفاظ على حقوقه والمطالبة باللقب حتى صدور الحكم النهائي. ووجّه مجلس الإدارة رسالة إلى الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم، أكد خلالها أن المريخ يمتلك تاريخًا كبيرًا ومكانة جماهيرية ورياضية داخل السودان وخارجه، ولن يسمح بالمساس بحقوقه أو الانتقاص من مكتسباته، مشددًا على ضرورة تحمل الاتحاد مسؤولياته في إدارة المسابقات وفقًا لمبادئ العدالة والنزاهة والحياد. كما طالب النادي الاتحاد السوداني بتطبيق اللوائح والقوانين على جميع الأندية دون تمييز أو انتقائية، مؤكدًا أنه لن يقبل فرض أي قرارات كأمر واقع، وأنه سيستخدم كافة الوسائل القانونية والمؤسسية المتاحة للدفاع عن حقوقه. واختتم المريخ بيانه بتوجيه رسالة إلى جماهيره، شدد خلالها على أن حقوق النادي ليست قابلة للتفاوض أو التنازل، وأن مجلس الإدارة مستمر في اتخاذ المسارات القانونية حتى النهاية، معربًا عن ثقته في مساندة جماهيره خلال المرحلة المقبلة، أن موقفه يزداد تعقيدا في ظل تلقيه إخطارا رسميا من الاتحاد السوداني يفيد بانتقال النزاع إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية، على خلفية الشكوى المقدمة من الهلال تحت رقم A/12688، معتبرًا أن ذلك يطرح تساؤلات بشأن الأساس القانوني لإعادة فتح الملف أمام لجنة الاستئنافات. وأكد مجلس إدارة النادي اتخاذه قرارًا باللجوء إلى المحكمة الرياضية الدولية، واستكمال جميع الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة للدفاع عن حق الفريق في اللقب، مشيرا إلى أنه سيستعين بمتخصصين في القضايا الرياضية، مستندًا إلى خبراته السابقة أمام المحكمة. وشدد المريخ على أن حقوق النادي ومكتسباته ليست محل تفريط، مطالبًا الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم بتحمل مسؤولياته في إدارة المسابقة، والالتزام بمبادئ العدالة والحياد وتطبيق اللوائح على جميع الأندية دون تمييز أو انتقائية. كما وجه مجلس الإدارة رسالة إلى جماهير النادي ورموزه ونجومه ووسائل الإعلام المحسوبة عليه، أكد خلالها تمسكه بموقفه القانوني ومواصلة الدفاع عن حقوق المريخ حتى صدور حكم نهائي ينهي الجدل المثار حول هوية بطل المسابقة. وتعود أزمة لقب الدوري السوداني إلى الموسم الماضي، بعدما حصل المريخ على البطولة رغم خسارته أمام الهلال بهدف دون مقابل في الجولة الأخيرة، وذلك عقب قبول الاستئناف الذي تقدم به ضد قانونية مشاركة عدد من لاعبي الهلال في مباراة القمة، وهو القرار الذي منح football.summary: أعلن نادي المريخ السوداني تصعيد أزمة لقب الدوري الممتاز إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية "كاس"، بعد رفضه قرار لجنة الاستئنافات بالاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم الذي منح غريمه الهلال لقب الدوري. جاء هذا القرار بعد أن قررت اللجنة نقض الحكم السابق الذي كان لصالح المريخ، مما أثار استغراب إدارة النادي التي أكدت أن اللجنة السابقة كانت قد أقرت بأحقية المريخ في اللقب. وأشار المريخ إلى أن النزاع قد انتقل رسميًا إلى "كاس" بسبب الشكوى المقدمة من الهلال، مما يطرح تساؤلات حول الأساس القانوني لإعادة فتح الملف. وأكد النادي أنه سيتخذ جميع الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة للدفاع عن حقوقه، مشددًا على أهمية الالتزام بمبادئ العدالة والحياد في إدارة المسابقة. كما طمأن جماهيره بأنه سيواصل الدفاع عن حقه حتى صدور حكم نهائي.

منوعات 🌓 بعد قرار سحب الدوري ومنحه لـ الهلال.. المريخ السوداني يصعد إلى المحكمة الرياضية إقرأ التفاصيل المريخ السوداني يرفض قرار لجنة الاستئناف بشأن لقب الدوري للموسم الماضي، ويعلن تصعيد القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية كاس إيمان السيد 🕒 منذ 16 ساعة تابعنا على جوجل بعد قرار سحب الدوري ومنحه لـ الهلال.. المريخ السوداني يصعد إلى المحكمة الرياضية أعلن نادي المريخ السوداني رفضه قرار لجنة الاستئناف المتعلق بلقب الدوري للموسم الماضي، مؤكداً أنه سيتجه إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية «كاس» للطعن في القرار. وكان نادي الهلال السوداني قد أعلن مساء الثلاثاء حصوله على لقب الدوري السوداني للموسم الماضي، بقرار رسمي صادر عن لجنة الاستئناف في الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم . وقال المريخ في بيانه الرسمي، الصادر عبر صفحاته الرسمية، إنه يرفض «القاطع» قرار لجنة الاستئنافات المشكلة حديثًا، والقاضي بقبول طلب الفحص المقدم من النادي الآخر، ونقض القرار السابق الذي قضى بأحقية المريخ في لقب بطولة الدوري الممتاز. وأضاف البيان أن النادي يتمسك بكافة حقوقه ومكتسباته، ويرفض أي إجراءات تنتقص منها، مشيرًا إلى أن القرار الأخير يثير استغراب المجلس، خاصة أن لجنة الاستئنافات السابقة كانت قد أصدرت قرارها لصالح المريخ وأشادت في حيثياته بالاستئناف الذي تقدم به النادي. وأوضح المريخ أن الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم أجرى تعديلات على لائحة أوضاع اللاعبين استنادًا إلى ما انتهت إليه اللجنة في القضية، معتبرًا أن العدول عن ذلك القرار يثير تساؤلات قانونية. وأشار البيان إلى أن النادي تلقى إخطارًا رسميًا من الاتحاد يفيد بانتقال القضية إلى محكمة التحكيم الرياضية الدولية «CAS»، بناءً على الشكوى المقدمة من النادي الآخر بالرقم A/12688، وهو ما دفع مجلس الإدارة إلى حسم أمره والتصعيد إلى المحكمة الرياضية. واختتم المريخ بيانه بالتأكيد على أنه سيواصل الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة دفاعًا عن حقه في البطولة حتى صدور القرار النهائي، داعيًا الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم إلى الالتزام بمسؤولياته في إدارة المنافسة بعدالة وحياد وتطبيق اللوائح دون تمييز أو انتقائية. وكان الدوري السوداني قد حُسم الموسم الماضي بشكل مثير للجدل، بعدما توج المريخ باللقب رغم فوز الهلال بهدف نظيف في الجولة الأخيرة، وذلك بعد قبول استئناف المريخ ضد قرار لجنة المسابقات بشأن قانونية مشاركة عدد من لاعبي الهلال في مباراة القمة بين الفريقين. ✓ فحص وتدقيق «إقرأ نيوز»: ✔️ صحيح إلى حد كبير 📌 الادعاء المتداول: المريخ السوداني يرفض قرار لجنة
